q: The Costa dirty-paper coding (DPC) result states that for the channel Y = X + S + Z (S is interference known to encoder, Z ~ N(0,N), power constraint P on X):
opts: The capacity is log(1 + P/(N + σ²_S))
The capacity is the same as if S were absent: C = ½ log(1 + P/N)
The capacity is reduced by the interference
exp: Costa (1983): if the encoder knows S non-causally, the channel capacity is ½ log(1+P/N)—as if S were absent! The encoder pre-cancels the known interference using a version of Gel'fand-Pinsker coding (auxiliary variable U = X + αS). This underlies precoding in MIMO communications.
